models_evaluated: Google Cloud AutoML Vision Image Classification Down Syndrome Detection model

links.outcome: Effect of adjusting confidence threshold on Down Syndrome detection sensitivity
links.effect: Adjusting the confidence threshold gave 100% sensitivity at the cost of more false positives; default threshold 0.5 gave precision 86.67%, recall 92.86%.
links.quote: On adjustment of software parameters (the confidence threshold of prediction), the technique can deliver highly accurate Down Syndrome diagnosis with a 100% Sensitivity, at the expense of false positives that may be ruled out through further confirmatory testing.

links.outcome: Local performance of the model on Indian children versus 98%+ controlled-experiment accuracy
links.effect: Sensitivity 100%, specificity 80%, average precision 96.6%, precision 86.67%, recall 92.86% at threshold 0.5, versus 98%+ accuracy in the controlled experiment.
links.quote: The CloudML model trained with 104 images initially achieved: Sensitivity - 100%, specificity - 80%, Average Precision - 96.6%, precision - 86.67%, and Recall - 92.86% (Precision and Recall are calculated at a confidence threshold of 0.5)

screen.reason: The study tests the clinical validity and accuracy of a facial image classification model in a clinical setting in the hands of parents/end-users, but primarily evaluates diagnostic accuracy rather than testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
